title: How to Play Color Nonograms: Clues, Colors & First Moves
excerpt: Color nonograms use one clue group per color. Learn how to read colored numbers, handle touching blocks, and solve your first board.
body:
# How to Play Color Nonograms

A color nonogram uses the same grid and the same idea as a black-and-white one. The numbers still tell you how many cells to fill, but each one is printed in the color of the run it describes. A single row might hold a red group, then a blue group, then a yellow group, in that order.

If black-and-white nonograms are new to you, read [how to play nonogram](/guides/how-to-play-nonogram) first. Only two things here are genuinely different.

![A three-color nonogram with color-matched clues](/assets/og/nonogram-05-color-nonogram.png "806x698")

## Rule 1: the number's color is part of the clue

On a classic board, `2 1` means a run of two followed later by a run of one. On a color board, a red `2` followed by a blue `1` means exactly that, in the same reading order: left to right or top to bottom.

Change the colors and the answer changes too. You have to read the ink as well as the digit.

## Rule 2: same-color runs need a gap, different-color runs may touch

Two runs of the **same** color in one line must have at least one empty cell between them. Two runs of **different** colors can sit side by side with no gap at all.

That second part catches most beginners out. On the 8×8 board above, the middle rows run blue → red → yellow → red → blue with no empty cells between several of the groups. Perfectly legal.

> Some puzzle implementations use stricter rules and require a gap between every run. Check the rule screen of the game you're playing if a board seems impossible. Most standard color nonograms allow different colors to touch.

## How to start a color board

**Step 1 — pick one color and ignore the rest.** Treat the board as a black-and-white puzzle where only that color counts. Every cell of a different color is simply not this color, and it acts as a blank for your counting.

**Step 2 — apply the usual counting.** A line with a red `4` in an 8-wide grid gives you the same overlap and minimum-space logic you already know. Add the numbers, add the gaps between same-color groups, and compare with the line length.

**Step 3 — lock the forced cells, then switch color.** Once one color has given you all it can, move to the next. Filling color A often forces color B straight away, because the remaining spaces in a line have to be distributed differently.

**Step 4 — cross-check in both directions.** A red cell is confirmed by the row clue and the column clue of the same color. Use both, the same way you would on a classic board.

The first color board I tried took far too long, and the reason was simple. I kept putting gaps between red and blue runs. I'd solve one color at a time now, every time.

## Counting with colored clues

The formula is unchanged, but count only one color at a time:

> Minimum cells for one color = sum of that color's clue numbers + (number of runs of that color − 1)

A red `3 2` needs 3 + 1 + 2 = 6 cells of space. Those cells don't have to be adjacent in the finished picture, since other colors may sit between the groups when the rules allow different colors to touch. The red runs themselves still need at least one non-red cell between them.

## Mistakes that cost the most time

- Reading the number but ignoring its color. This is the common one by a long way.
- Inserting a gap between two different-colored runs. You'll rule out the correct answer.
- Assuming the color groups in a line must fill every cell. Empty cells are still allowed.
- Trying to solve all colors at once. Work one layer at a time.
- Forgetting that a cell can hold only one color.

## How color nonograms compare for difficulty

Slightly, at first. You're doing the same work for two or three layers, and the different-colors-may-touch rule takes away a shortcut you may have come to rely on. After a handful of boards it becomes routine. Most players find 8×8 color puzzles easier than 15×15 black-and-white ones.

## Try a color board

[Nonogram Collection](/game/nonogram-collection) has a dedicated Color mode alongside classic boards, paired Clip puzzles, oversized Mega boards and triangle-shaped Triddlers. It runs in the browser with no download, and completed pictures are saved to an in-game album.

body:
# How to Play Nonogram on Android

You don't need an app store to play nonograms on Android. A browser-based game runs on your phone with the same rules as the desktop version. The only adjustment worth thinking about is how you fill cells with a finger instead of a mouse.

If you are still learning the clues, start with [the step-by-step nonogram guide](/guides/how-to-play-nonogram). This page is about the controls and the small-screen workflow.

![A nonogram being solved on an Android phone](/assets/og/nonogram-06-android-phone.png "430x700")

## Browser game versus Android app

Both work. Here's how they differ.

- **Browser.** Nothing to install, no storage taken up, and updates arrive on their own. You can open the same puzzle on a laptop later. Progress is usually saved in the browser itself.
- **App.** You may get offline play and a bigger board view, but it takes space and often comes with ads or a sign-in prompt.

For most players, the browser route is quicker. [Nonogram Collection](/game/nonogram-collection) runs directly in Chrome, Edge or Firefox on Android, with 109 puzzles across five modes and a new daily puzzle. No download, no account.

## Touch controls that actually matter

**Drag to fill.** Don't tap 15 cells one by one. Press the first cell and slide your finger along the row. Most browser nonograms paint a whole run in one gesture, and that's the biggest speed improvement you'll get on a phone.

**Use the cross tool.** On desktop you can right-click to mark a cell empty. On a touchscreen there is no right-click, so switch to the cross/X tool in the toolbar, then tap the cells you know are blank. Nonogram Collection has the tool switcher on screen, and a long-press works in plenty of other games too.

**Undo is your safety net.** A misplaced drag can ruin several cells at once. After every big gesture, glance at the result and undo immediately if it went too far.

**Zoom before you commit.** On a 15×15 board, pinch to zoom or turn the phone sideways. I tried one in portrait once and gave up after five minutes. Landscape fixed it.

**Keep the crosses.** It's tempting to clear the marks once the picture starts to appear. Don't. The crosses are what let you solve the remaining lines without starting over.

## Playing on Android 10 and older phones

If you searched for “how to play nonogram Android 10”, the short answer is that the Android version rarely matters. A modern browser on Android 10 handles these puzzle pages fine, because the game runs in the browser instead of relying on device-specific code.

A few practical notes for older devices:

- Keep the browser updated. An old Chrome build is more likely to cause layout problems than the operating system.
- If the page feels slow, turn off dark mode in the game's settings. It helps on some OLED screens and can reduce contrast on older LCD panels.
- Want an app-like icon? Use the browser's **Add to Home Screen** option. It's a shortcut rather than a real install, and takes almost no space.
- Don't clear browser data between sessions if you want to keep your saved progress. Browser games usually store it locally.

## Small-screen checklist

1. Start with 5×5 or 10×10 boards before attempting 15×15.
2. Use landscape orientation for grids wider than 10 cells.
3. Turn screen-rotation lock off while playing.
4. Use drag-to-fill, and the cross tool for blanks.
5. Take a break every 10 minutes. These puzzles are easy on the eyes, and the neck is what suffers.

## Where to play

[Nonogram Collection](/game/nonogram-collection) covers classic, color, Clip, Mega and Triddler boards in one browser page. Fill by dragging, mark blanks with the cross tool, undo, reset, spend a star on a hint, and revisit the daily puzzle. Everything is saved in the browser, so you can close the tab and come back later.

title: How to Redeem RO CAM Codes: Step by Step
excerpt: How to redeem RO CAM codes in four steps. Open the in-game tablet with T, go to PROGRESS, then CODES, and paste the code. Fixes for codes that won't work.
body:
**The short answer:** Press `T` in RO CAM to open your tablet, tap `PROGRESS`, then `CODES`, paste the code into the box, and hit `REDEEM`. The Marks appear in your balance immediately.

Once you know where the menu is, there's not much to it. The tablet is the part that catches people out, because it isn't a Roblox menu and it isn't on the main screen. You have to be inside the game first.

![The four-step RO CAM redemption flow](/assets/og/ro-cam-02-redeem-flow.png "800x340")

## Step 1 — Launch RO CAM

Open RO CAM through Roblox and load into the game. You need to reach the lobby or the patrol spawn. The tablet menu isn't available on the title screen.

## Step 2 — Press T to open the tablet

Press the `T` key on your keyboard. A tablet interface opens with your operator menus on it. This is where all the code stuff lives.

On a phone or tablet, use the on-screen control that opens the same menu. The `T` shortcut is a keyboard thing.

## Step 3 — Go to PROGRESS, then CODES

At the top of the tablet, tap `PROGRESS`. Inside that tab, pick `CODES`. You'll see a text box waiting for a code.

## Step 4 — Paste and redeem

Paste your code in and hit `REDEEM`. If the code is good, the Marks land in your balance straight away. No confirmation screen, no waiting.

Codes are case-sensitive. `3kccu` is lowercase; `1MILLIONVISITS` is uppercase. Swap the case and it fails. Copy them from [the full working code list](/codes/ro-cam-codes) instead of typing.

## Why your RO CAM code isn't working

I've had codes bounce back for three reasons, and the first one is by far the most common.

**Wrong capitalization.** The game treats `3kccu` and `3KCCU` as different codes. Paste, don't type.

**A typo somewhere in the middle.** `1MILLIONVISITS` is easy to mistype. Check the spelling against the list before you try again.

**The code expired.** Less likely with RO CAM, since the game launched in November 2026 and no codes have expired yet. If a code does fail after you've checked the case and spelling, it's probably dead.

If none of those apply, restart the game and try once more. Sometimes the tablet menu needs a reload.

## What Marks are for

Marks buy guns, vests, helmets, attachments and operator gear. You begin with a basic Hi-Point and unlock the rest with Marks. [Here's what I'd buy first](/codes/ro-cam-marks).

## Play something similar

RO CAM is Roblox-only. The closest browser shooters we cover are [ObbloxGun.io 3D FPS Shooter](/game/obbloxgun-io-3d-fps-shooter) and [Armed Forces.io](/game/armed-forces-io); more code lists live in the [codes hub](/codes).

title: RO CAM Marks: What They Buy and How to Get More
excerpt: What Marks do in RO CAM, what to buy first, and how to earn more. Includes the seven working codes worth 11,500 Marks combined.
body:
Marks are the money in RO CAM. You spend them on guns, vests, helmets, attachments and operator gear. You start with a basic Hi-Point, so almost every upgrade in the game comes down to Marks.

I'll be straight with you: the game hands out Marks through codes faster than it does through normal play right now. The seven live codes are worth 11,500 Marks, which buys a lot of gear for a few minutes of work.

![What Marks buy in RO CAM](/assets/og/ro-cam-03-marks-spending.png "760x440")

## What Marks buy in RO CAM

| Category | What you get |
|---|---|
| Firearms | The rest of the 30+ gun roster, beyond the starting Hi-Point |
| Armor | Tactical vests and helmets for higher-risk patrols |
| Attachments | Sights, grips and other loadout upgrades |
| Operator gear | Kits, patches and customization items |

Vests and helmets are the ones I'd prioritize. Gun play is fun, but dying on a high-risk patrol because you skipped body armor costs more time than a new sight saves.

## How to get Marks in RO CAM

**Redeem the codes.** Seven are live as of 2026-11-28, worth 11,500 Marks total. `3kccu` alone pays 3,000. [Here's the full list](/codes/ro-cam-codes), and [here's how to redeem them](/codes/how-to-redeem-ro-cam-codes) if the tablet menu isn't obvious.

**Play the game.** Patrols and high-risk scenarios pay Marks. It's slower than codes, but it's the steady source once the codes run out.

**Watch for milestone drops.** RO CAM's codes follow player counts and visit counts. `1MILLIONVISITS` and `500KVISITS` are the obvious examples. More milestones mean more free Marks if you keep an eye on the [code page](/codes/ro-cam-codes).

## What to buy first

If you've got 11,500 Marks from the codes, that's enough to change how the game plays. I'd go in this order:

1. A vest and helmet, so you survive more than one bad encounter.
2. A primary gun you actually like, rather than the starting pistol.
3. Attachments for that gun.
4. Operator kits and patches last. They're nice, but they don't keep you alive.

Your mileage may vary if you mostly play Gun Game. The priority list assumes you're doing patrols.
